quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to stay safe. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see farther down the road. Be flexible with your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT cause a motorcycle wobble?
questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to accelerate out of a wobble.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, what should you do?

options.text: Move as far to the right as possible.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the center of your lane. Riding toward the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding away from them may cause the driver to merge back too soon. The center position is safest.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Talk to your passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to your passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle responds more slowly. With a passenger, ride slower, slow down sooner, and increase following distance. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When do most crashes happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: Which formation should a group use when entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for groups to stay close while keeping safe distance. Use single-file for curves, turns, and highway exits or entries.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Place inexperienced riders at the back.
Not ride too close to other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride too close to other riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation and check mirrors often. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Keep safe distance between all riders in the group.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file line.
questions.explanation: Three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for staggered formation. Groups of three-wheel motorcycles should travel in a single-file line.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to get a motorcycle (M) endorsement?
questions.correctAnswerText: 18 years old.
questions.explanation: In the District of Columbia, you must be at least 18 years old to get a motorcycle (M) endorsement on your driver license.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket while riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take breaks to remove it and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep riders cool in warm weather.
No, jackets make it hard to steer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep riders cool in warm weather.
questions.explanation: A riding jacket helps prevent dehydration and protects you in all weather. Many jackets are made to protect riders from overheating, even in warm weather.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is not recommended because it causes heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is light-colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They provide safety protection and can help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then re-apply it.
Release the brake and use only the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until the motorcycle comes to a full stop.

questions.question: If you carry a load in a sidecar, the motorcycle's stopping distance:

options.text: Will be the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: May increase.
questions.explanation: Adding weight to a motorcycle increases its inertia, which can make stopping distance longer. Start slowing down earlier when carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: Before a passenger rides, you should instruct them to do everything except:

options.text: Get on after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay far away from you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to mount the motorcycle after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as they can without crowding you and hold onto the handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. Press the opposite handgrip to return to your original direction after you pass the hazard.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, try to hit it at close to a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible, keep the motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and ease off the throttle just before impact.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane for safety. Riding near the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding far from the passing driver may cause them to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: In normal riding conditions, maintain a following distance of at least:
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds between you and the vehicle ahead in normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Which is a bad reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the car ahead too closely.
Someone is sitting in the driver's seat of a parked car.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a person walking in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn before passing a vehicle or pedestrian who might move into your lane. If a nearby driver is too close to the car ahead, they may try to pass and cut in front of you. If someone sits in a parked car or a pedestrian is in the street, use your horn as you pass. Do not use your horn just to get attention.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to drive, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Get other friends to talk them out of driving.
Arrange a different way for them to get home.
Tell them to drive on quiet roads instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to drive on quiet roads instead.
questions.explanation: Do not suggest they drive on less busy roads. Instead, arrange another way home, keep them busy to slow their drinking, make excuses to stop them from leaving, or get friends to help talk them out of driving.

questions.question: When someone passes you from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: If your front wheel starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Keep the front brake on and ride it out.
Keep the front brake on and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader, near the front of the group. This lets experienced riders watch them without making the inexperienced rider lead.
